Prevention: Plant early and avoid planting the crop very close to each other
Practise deep ploughing and harrow to kill larvae/pupae or expose them to direct sunlight and predators
Plant castor crop (barrier crop) in 3 rows with close spacing (50cm) around the field, one month earlier before planting green grams
Remove and destroy volunteer green gram plants which may harbour the pod borer
Rotate or intercrop green gram with non host crop e.g. maize, sourghum, millet or sunflower
Monitoring: Monitor the crops frequently as there is only a brief period from hatching to entering buds or pods
Check for damaged pods which have small, darkened circular entry holes
Inspect the leaves, buds and pods which are mostly webbed together.
The caterpillar feeds inside the web
Look out on flowers for any discolouration and damaged or missing reproductive parts
Take action when damage holes are seen on 2-4 plants
Direct Control: This helps when their numbers are low and in small fields
Remove and destroy by burning or burying in a 30 cm pit all affected plants
Install pheromone traps 50 m apart @5 traps/ha, install bird perches @50/ha from the beginning of pod maturity
Create a conducive environment for natural enemies (e.g lady bird beetles, spiders, praying mantis etc.) to multiply by growing hedges of flowering plants
Restrictions: When using a pesticide, always wear protective clothing and follow the instructions on the product label
Do not use chemicals with the same mode of action year after year as this can lead to resistance
Always consult the most recent list of registered pesticides (PCPB)
Product unlikely to present hazard under conditions of normal use.
No more than 1 spray during flowering.
